title: Fake Bank SMS
articleHeadline: Fake Bank SMS Scams Continue to Target Customers
author: Scam Advisory Team
description: Scammers impersonate bank notifications and ask victims to click a fake login link.
recommendedActions: Verify with the official banking app

overview: Bank impersonation messages are one of the most common scam formats used to create urgency.
They try to trick users into sharing credentials or OTP codes by mimicking legitimate service messages.
howItWorks: Scammers send a message that appears to come from a reputable bank.
The message prompts users to click a link or enter login details on a fake page.
steps: A message claims an account issue or payment problem.
The user is directed to a fraudulent webpage.
Credentials or authorization codes are collected by the scammer.
warningSigns: Urgent threats to close the account
protectionTips: Type the bank's official website directly into your browser.
Contact the bank using a verified phone number.
whatToDo: Preserve any evidence and report the scam.

title: Recruitment Fee Job Scam
articleHeadline: Fake Recruiters Ask for Upfront Fees Before Interviews
author: Scam Advisory Team
description: Fake job offers ask candidates to pay recruitment fees before scheduling interviews.

overview: Job scams often promise high salaries and fast hiring timelines.
They ask candidates to pay fees for background checks or application processing.
howItWorks: Fraudsters reach out with a job offer that seems too good to be true.
They ask for money before the candidate can move forward.
steps: A candidate receives an unsolicited offer.
The recruiter asks for payment to continue.
The job offer disappears after payment is made.
protectionTips: Never send money for job applications.
whatToDo: Report the scheme to the authorities.

title: Crypto Investment Pitch
articleHeadline: Crypto Investment Scam Promises Guaranteed Returns
author: Scam Advisory Team
description: A social media ad promises quick crypto returns and asks users to fund a wallet.
recommendedActions: Report the post to the platform.

overview: Investment scams are often shared through social media or messaging apps.
They promise large profits with little or no risk.
howItWorks: Scammers entice users with impressive returns.
Victims are directed to transfer funds to a wallet they control.
steps: A targeted ad or message offers a crypto opportunity.
The victim sends money to a suspicious wallet.
The scammer disappears and the funds are lost.
protectionTips: Never send funds to unknown wallets.
whatToDo: Contact your bank or wallet provider.
Report the scam to the platform.
